text.p: Following are the main stories in Wednesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
All dailies lead with Malaysian Cabinet accepting Singapore Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew's apology and offer to retract his disparaging remarks on Malaysia's Johor state.
-- Four Royal Malaysian Air Force personnel were killed and seven others were feared dead after two helicopters crashed within minutes of each in Sabah state.
-- The Cabinet decides that all companies intending to sign memoranda of understanding with foreign parties to undertake ventures overseas must register with the Malaysian embassies.
-- Malaysia wins extra landing rights to Osaka, Nagoya and Fukuoka in Japan.
-- Transport Minister Ling Liong Sik says state railway firm KTB Bhd's land in Singapore will remain with Malaysia for 999 years.
